items.title: A Prompt-Injection Firewall for AI Agents and RAG Pipelines
items.raw_excerpt:
We built SafeBrowse — an open-source prompt-injection firewall for AI systems. Instead of relying on better prompts, SafeBrowse enforces a hard security boundary between untrusted web content and LLMs. It blocks hidden instructions, policy violations, and poisoned data before the AI ever sees it. Features:
• Prompt injection detection (50+ patterns)
• Policy engine (login/payment blocking)
• Fail-closed by design
• Audit logs & request IDs • Python SDK (sync + async)
• RAG sanitization PyPI: pip install safebrowse Looking for feedback from AI infra, security, and agent builders.

items.title: 从「工具」到「搭档」，AI4S 走过深水区 | 2025年终回顾
items.raw_excerpt: 在这一轮波澜壮阔的人工智能浪潮中，我们常被算力、模型规模和颠覆式叙事所簇拥。然而，真正值得记录的变化，往往发生在那些远离喧嚣的实验室里、发生在一行行代码与科学假设的碰撞中：AI 是如何从一种“使能技术”，演变为改变人类推进科研的基本范式的？ 2025年，AI4Science（AI4S）不再仅仅是论文中的愿景。它正以一种极其务实且具体的姿态，嵌入到每一位科学家的日常。 在这一年里，我们看到 AI4S 呈现出多维度的进化： 它是高效的“科研加速器”： 从润色论文到整理会议纪要，从自动化数据处理到启发科学假设，正如吴琦教授与许东教授所言，AI 正在将科学家从低效的试错中解放，让他们重新聚焦于“创造性思维”本身。 它是认知的“破局者”： 无论是 AlphaFold 3 的持续震撼，还是 Noetik 的虚拟细胞模型，AI 开始突破传统学科的藩篱。樊隽轩教授与张清鹏教授都观察到，当数据被转化为 AI 可理解的要素，两个独立领域被真正贯通，认知的“红利”正加速转化为科研的“生产力”。 它是未来的“自主探索者”： 尽管如张晓峰教授所指，AI Scientist 尚处初级阶段，但“自动化发现”（Automation）已成为杜沅岂等年轻学者眼中的确定未来。 正如李国杰院士在寄语中所指出：AI4S 正在让思维本身成为可工程化的对象。如果说 2024 年是 AI 获得科学界最高荣誉诺贝尔奖的加冕礼，那么 2025 年则是 AI 深入科研的“现场记录”。 步入 2026 年，我们不仅关注模型能力的突破，更期待“AI 专家”与“学科专家”的深度共融，期待鄂维南院士所构想的“超级实验室”与开源共享生态的落地。 为此，雷峰网邀请了来自顶级高校及一线科研机构的多位AI 专家与学科专家，通过他们的亲历与洞察，还原一个真实、诚恳且充满可能性的 AI4S 2025。这不仅是一次年度总结，更是一份通往“

excerpt_i18n.en:
In this sweeping wave of artificial intelligence, we are often surrounded by discussions of computing power, model scale, and disruptive narratives. Yet, the truly noteworthy changes often occur in quiet laboratories, in the collision between lines of code and scientific hypotheses: How has AI evolved from an "enabling technology" to fundamentally reshaping the way humans advance scientific research? By 2025, AI4Science (AI4S) is no longer just a vision in academic papers. It is embedding itself into the daily work of every scientist in an extremely practical and concrete manner.

This year, we see AI4S evolving across multiple dimensions:

It serves as an efficient "research accelerator": From polishing papers to organizing meeting notes, from automating data processing to inspiring scientific hypotheses, as noted by Professors Wu Qi and Xu Dong, AI is freeing scientists from inefficient trial and error, allowing them to refocus on "creative thinking" itself.

It acts as a cognitive "game-changer": Whether through the continued impact of AlphaFold 3 or Noetik’s virtual cell models, AI is beginning to break through the barriers of traditional disciplines. Professors Fan Junxuan and Zhang Qingpeng have observed that when data is transformed into elements understandable by AI, two independent fields are truly connected, accelerating the conversion of cognitive "dividends" into research "productivity."

It is emerging as a future "autonomous explorer": Although, as Professor Zhang Xiaofeng points out, the AI Scientist is still in its early stages, the era of "automated discovery" is quietly approaching.
excerpt_i18n.es: En esta impresionante ola de inteligencia artificial, a menudo nos vemos rodeados por la potencia de cálculo, la escala de los modelos y las narrativas disruptivas. Sin embargo, los cambios verdaderamente dignos de registro suelen ocurrir en esos laboratorios alejados del bullicio, en la colisión entre líneas de código e hipótesis científicas: ¿cómo ha evolucionado la IA desde ser una "tecnología habilitadora" hasta transformar el paradigma fundamental de la investigación científica? En 2025, AI4Science (AI4S) ya no es solo una visión en los artículos académicos. Se está integrando en el día a día de cada científico de una manera extremadamente práctica y concreta. Este año, hemos observado que AI4S presenta una evolución multidimensional: es un "asistente de investigación" eficiente.

While autonomous driving systems learn to perform 4D modeling, reconstruction, and resimulation of these dynamic objects, most solutions still rely on per-scene optimization, known camera calibration, or short-frame windows, making them slow and impractical. The ability to quickly and cost-effectively obtain simulation data in dynamic driving scenarios determines the evolution speed of autonomous driving systems in the open world. excerpt_i18n.en:
Skyris was originally inspired by a guinea pig named Tuntun. It was the most homebody pet Zhang Yunuo ever had, spending its days lying among a group of young entrepreneurs, rarely moving, quietly accepting praise and petting. At the time, Zhang Yunuo was working on delivery drones in the United States when a friend suddenly asked him, why can’t guinea pigs fly? Tuntun never took off, but the combination of flight and pets perfectly aligned the two pieces of Skyris. Or perhaps Zhang Yunuo had always wanted to focus on pets; the voice box is as homebound as a guinea pig, and flight merely gives them the ability to actively provide companionship, much like what Zhang Yunuo felt from his other pets.  

Zhang Yunuo has kept many pets: five dogs, three cats, one snake, one guinea pig, and soon, a parrot. The story began when he was five years old, when a Tibetan Mastiff almost as tall as himself became his companion. At the time, Zhang Yunuo was still afraid of dogs. He ran, and it chased, until his legs could no longer move, and “being eaten” seemed like an option. Zhang Yunuo lay on the ground, giving up. But the Tibetan Mastiff just trotted over with its large head, looked at him, and then lowered its head to lick his face.  

“From then on, I was never afraid of dogs again. I knew it wouldn’t hurt me.” Zhang Yunuo decided to name it Jinjin.  

Zhang Yunuo has always felt that the true companionship he experienced came from these pets. Sometimes, self-expression leads to loneliness, and in moments of being misunderstood, anyone can become an “outsider” among others. Studying, starting a business… Zhang Yunuo repeatedly experienced these moments at different stages of his life.
excerpt_i18n.es: Según Skyris, la inspiración inicial provino del conejillo de indias holandés Tuntun. Era la mascota más hogareña que Zhang Yunuo había tenido, pasaba el día acostada entre un grupo de jóvenes emprendedores, rara vez se movía, aceptando silenciosamente elogios y caricias. En ese momento, Zhang Yunuo trabajaba en drones de entrega en Estados Unidos, y un día un amigo le preguntó de repente: ¿por qué no puede volar un conejillo de indias holandés? Tuntun finalmente no despegó, pero la combinación de vuelo y mascotas encajó perfectamente en las dos piezas del rompecabezas de Skyris. O tal vez, lo que Zhang Yunuo siempre quiso hacer fueron solo mascotas; la caja de voz es tan hogareña como un conejillo de indias holandés, y el vuelo simplemente les otorga la capacidad de acompañar activamente, tal como Zhang Yunuo había sentido con otras mascotas. Zhang Yunuo ha tenido muchas mascotas: cinco.

excerpt_i18n.en: On December 12, the eighth GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Summit officially commenced in Shenzhen. The two-day event was jointly organized by the GAIR Institute and Leiphone, with Academician Gao Wen serving as the chair of the steering committee, and Academician Yang Qiang and Professor Zhu Xiaorui as conference chairs. As a key window for observing the evolution of AI technology and ecosystem changes, the GAIR Summit has resonated with the pulse of global AI development since its inception in 2016, witnessing technological waves surge from laboratories into the depths of industry. In 2025, a critical juncture where large models transition from technological breakthroughs to value deepening, GAIR arrived as scheduled, collaborating with experts to explore the forefront of AI and gain insights into the underlying logic of the industry. At the summit, Dr. Xue Guirong, Chief Technology Officer of the Scientific Model Group at Zhejiang Laboratory and CEO of Tianrang Intelligence, delivered an engaging presentation. Dr. Xue pointed out that while AI technologies, represented by large language models, have shown potential in various disciplines, they remain inherently limited by the boundaries of language, struggling to truly understand high-dimensional, diverse scientific data or independently achieve verifiable scientific discoveries. Based on this, Dr. Xue systematically analyzed the fundamental differences between large language models and scientific foundation models, detailing the key advantages of the 021 scientific foundation model developed by Zhejiang Laboratory in transcending language dimensions, unifying scientific data, enabling scientific reasoning and discovery, and integrating interdisciplinary knowledge. He also raised considerations regarding AI for science.

Como una ventana crucial para observar la evolución tecnológica y los cambios en el ecosistema de la IA, la conferencia GAIR ha estado en sintonía con el pulso del desarrollo global de la IA desde su fundación en 2016, presenciando cómo las olas tecnológicas pasaron del laboratorio a la profundidad industrial. En 2025, un año clave en el que los grandes modelos transitan de "romper barreras técnicas" a "profundizar en el valor", GAIR llega puntualmente, uniendo a expertos para explorar la vanguardia de la IA.

excerpt_i18n.en: Leifeng.com exclusively learned that AI coding startup AIGCode recently completed consecutive rounds of financing led by Bohua Capital and Lihe Capital respectively, with Lihe Financial and multiple industrial capital investors participating. Gao Fei, a tenured associate professor and doctoral supervisor at the College of Control Science and Engineering, Zhejiang University, is an outstanding young scholar in this field. His research focuses include aerial robotics, autonomous navigation, swarm coordination, and embodied intelligence. He proposed the world's first autonomous flight swarm system for unstructured environments, published multiple papers in top-tier journals and conferences such as Science Robotics and TRO, and founded Differential AI Flight. Gao Fei is a recipient of the National Excellent Young Scientists Fund, has received multiple best paper nominations from IEEE TRO and IROS, and was named among the world's top 2% scientists in 2023-2024 and the MIT Technology Review's "35 Innovators Under 35" (MIT TR35) Asia Pacific list in 2025. Author: Qi Chengyong | Editor: Ma Xiaoning

Research on world models is still in its early stages, with no consensus yet formed. Studies in this field have branched into countless streams. Over the past year, video generation models, represented by Sora, have emerged as a new academic hotspot following large language models (LLMs). Essentially, the currently popular video generation models are a type of world model, with the core goal of generating realistic and coherent videos. To achieve this, the models must, to some extent, understand how the world operates (e.g., water flows downhill, the motion of objects after collision, reasonable human actions, etc.).

Hu Wenbo is undoubtedly a rising star in the field of world model research over the past two years. At the recently concluded GAIR 2025, Hu Wenbo, a senior researcher at Tencent ARC Lab, delivered a highly insightful speech titled "Towards 3D-aware Video World Models" at the GAIR conference organized by Leiphone.

The following is the detailed content, edited and organized by AI Tech Review without altering the original meaning.

Thank you for the invitation and introduction. The topic of my presentation today is "Towards 3D-aware Video World Models." I chose this topic because when Sora was released in early 2024, it greatly impressed everyone. For instance, the videos it generates, though appearing two-dimensional, already possess a certain level of 3D...
excerpt_i18n.es: Autor: Qi Chengyong. Editor: Ma Xiaoning. La investigación sobre modelos del mundo aún se encuentra en sus primeras etapas, sin que se haya alcanzado un consenso, generando innumerables ramas de estudio en este campo. En el último año, los modelos de generación de vídeo, representados por Sora, se han convertido en un nuevo foco académico tras los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM). En esencia, los populares modelos de generación de vídeo actuales son un tipo de modelo del mundo, cuyo objetivo central es producir vídeos realistas y coherentes. Para lograrlo, el modelo debe comprender, en cierta medida, cómo funciona el mundo (por ejemplo, que el agua fluye hacia abajo, el movimiento de objetos tras una colisión o las acciones humanas razonables). Hu Wenbo es precisamente una figura emergente absoluta en la investigación de modelos del mundo en los últimos dos años.
